title: A relayed root cause names the code line that acts, not a message string
why: Consultant 01:46 CST Nov 14 (relayed): it relayed a root cause (the merge-tool batch brake) from a cite string without reading the code path; the coordinator found merge.py:1658 says the opposite (see merge-brake-text-stale). The refusal text and BATCH_CITE still said the brake held; the code no longer enforced it.
source: Consultant 01:46 CST Nov 14 (relayed). Same family: act-claims-read-back (unstarted: a claim about an act is read back), the triage readings corrected on Nov 13 to 14 (#3279, the shard-order fix). A text string is a claim, not the code.
note: Triage 01:53 CST Nov 14: the consultant names the step for itself. The mistake: a cause taken from a message the code prints, not from the line that decides. The guard that would have stopped it: a report that names a cause names the file and line that acts, or says "text only, code unread". Not built, not queued beyond this step; the consultant owns the design. Not started.
